metadata.scope: Educational concept map; selected foundational concepts, not an exhaustive taxonomy.

encoding.title: Encoding and Information
encoding.define: Represent information, reduce its size, protect it from errors, secure it, and map it to physical signals.
encoding.notes: These are related operations with different objectives. Cryptography and modulation are included for comparison; neither is simply another character encoding.

representation.title: Representation Encoding
representation.define: Map values, symbols, or measurements to agreed representations.
representation.notes: Preserve meaning through a shared interpretation.

compression.title: Compression / Source Coding
compression.define: Reduce the number of bits needed to represent information.
compression.notes: Lossless coding preserves the original exactly; lossy coding trades fidelity for size.

error-control.title: Error Control / Channel Coding
error-control.define: Add structured redundancy to detect or correct transmission and storage errors.

cryptography.title: Cryptography
cryptography.define: Use cryptographic primitives and protocols for confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.
cryptography.notes: Encryption alone does not necessarily provide integrity or authentication.

physical.title: Physical-Layer Signaling
physical.define: Map data or messages to signals suitable for a physical medium.
physical.notes: Line coding, block transmission coding, and modulation solve different signaling problems.

numbers.title: Numerical Representation
numbers.define: Represent integers and real-valued quantities using finite bit patterns.

integers.title: Binary Integers
integers.define: Unsigned binary represents nonnegative integers; signed formats also represent negative values.

twos-complement.title: Two's Complement
twos-complement.define: Represent a signed integer with a negative weight on the most significant bit.
twos-complement.example: In 8 bits, 11111111 represents -1; the range is -128 to 127.

floating-point.title: Floating Point
floating-point.define: Represent a value using a sign, significand, and exponent.
floating-point.notes: Finite precision causes rounding. Many decimal fractions, including 0.1, have no exact finite binary representation.

characters.title: Characters and Text
characters.define: Distinguish abstract characters, code points, and encoded byte sequences.

ascii.title: ASCII
ascii.define: A 7-bit character code with 128 values, including letters, digits, punctuation, and control characters.
ascii.example: The character A has decimal code 65 (hexadecimal 41).

unicode.title: Unicode
unicode.define: A character standard that assigns code points and defines text properties and encoding forms.
unicode.example: A is U+0041; the euro sign is U+20AC.
unicode.notes: Unicode is not synonymous with UTF-8, and one visible character may contain multiple code points.

utf8.title: UTF-8
utf8.define: Encode Unicode scalar values as sequences of one to four bytes.
utf8.example: U+0041 becomes 41; U+20AC becomes E2 82 AC (hexadecimal).
utf8.notes: ASCII characters retain their one-byte ASCII values.

utf16.title: UTF-16
utf16.define: Encode Unicode scalar values using one or two 16-bit code units.
utf16.notes: Supplementary characters use surrogate pairs; byte order matters when code units are serialized.

media.title: Multimedia Representation
media.define: Represent sampled audio, images, and video as digital data.
media.notes: A media format may combine representation, compression, and container metadata.

pcm.title: Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM)
pcm.define: Sample a signal and quantize its amplitude into numerical values.
pcm.example: Uncompressed mono audio at 48,000 samples/s and 16 bits/sample uses 768,000 bits/s.
pcm.notes: Despite its name, PCM here concerns digitizing samples, not a radio carrier modulation scheme.

raster.title: Raster Images
raster.define: Represent an image as a grid of pixels with numerical channel values.

video.title: Digital Video
video.define: Represent a sequence of frames with timing information.
video.notes: Video codecs often exploit spatial and temporal redundancy.

spacetime.title: Space, Time, and Geography
spacetime.define: Represent positions and times with explicit units, reference systems, and conventions.

timestamps.title: Timestamps
timestamps.define: Represent an instant or local date-time using a documented time convention.
timestamps.notes: A local clock reading without a time zone may be ambiguous; an epoch count requires a unit and epoch definition.

coordinates.title: Geographic Coordinates
coordinates.define: Represent a position using coordinates tied to a coordinate reference system.
coordinates.notes: Latitude/longitude require a datum and axis order; height also requires a reference.

geohash.title: Geohash
geohash.define: Interleave quantized longitude and latitude bits and commonly encode them in Base32.
geohash.notes: A geohash identifies a spatial cell, not an exact point. It is not a cryptographic hash.

color.title: Color Representation
color.define: Represent colors using numerical components and an interpretation such as a color space.

rgb.title: RGB
rgb.define: Represent color with red, green, and blue components.
rgb.notes: RGB component values alone do not identify a color without a color space and transfer function.

ycbcr.title: YCbCr
ycbcr.define: Separate a luma component from two chroma components for digital image and video systems.
ycbcr.notes: Chroma subsampling can reduce color detail; conversion alone need not imply subsampling.

lossless.title: Lossless Compression
lossless.define: Recover the original input exactly from the compressed representation.
lossless.notes: No lossless compressor can shorten every possible input.

huffman.title: Huffman Coding
huffman.define: Assign prefix-free codewords based on symbol weights; frequent symbols tend to receive shorter codewords.
huffman.notes: Optimal among binary symbol-by-symbol prefix codes for the given weights; each codeword has an integer bit length.

arithmetic.title: Arithmetic Coding
arithmetic.define: Represent a symbol sequence by progressively narrowing an interval according to a probability model.
arithmetic.notes: Can approach fractional-bit average costs across a sequence; encoder and decoder must agree on the model.

dictionary.title: Dictionary Coding
dictionary.define: Replace repeated strings with references to previously seen or stored strings.
dictionary.example: LZ77 uses references to earlier text in a sliding window.

rle.title: Run-Length Encoding
rle.define: Represent a run of repeated values by the value and a count.
rle.example: AAAAABBB can be represented conceptually as (A,5), (B,3).

lossy.title: Lossy Compression
lossy.define: Discard selected information to reduce size while meeting a distortion or perceptual target.

quantization.title: Quantization
quantization.define: Map many input values to a smaller set of representative values.
quantization.notes: Quantization is generally irreversible and also occurs when digitizing physical measurements.

transform.title: Transform Coding
transform.define: Transform samples into coefficients that can be quantized and coded efficiently.
transform.notes: The transform need not itself be lossy; quantization commonly causes the loss.

perceptual.title: Perceptual Coding
perceptual.define: Use properties of perception to allocate fewer bits to less noticeable information.
perceptual.example: Audio coding can exploit masking; image coding can allocate bits unevenly across frequencies.

detection.title: Error Detection
detection.define: Determine whether received data violates a coding constraint; detection alone does not locate or repair every error.

parity.title: Parity Bit
parity.define: Add a bit so the total number of one bits has a chosen parity.
parity.notes: Detects every odd number of bit flips, but can miss an even number.

crc.title: Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC)
crc.define: Compute a polynomial remainder over binary data to detect specified classes of errors.
crc.notes: Detection guarantees depend on the generator polynomial and message length. CRC is not protection against intentional tampering.

correction.title: Forward Error Correction
correction.define: Recover data from some corrupted received words using structured redundancy without requesting retransmission.

linear-block.title: Linear Block Codes
linear-block.define: Map fixed-length messages to codewords forming a linear subspace over a finite field.
linear-block.notes: A linear (n,k) code carries k symbols in n transmitted symbols; its rate is k/n.

hamming.title: Hamming Codes
hamming.define: A family of binary linear block codes with minimum distance 3 that can correct one bit error.
hamming.example: Hamming (7,4) encodes 4 data bits into 7 bits.
hamming.notes: Adding an overall parity bit yields an extended code with distance 4, commonly used for single-error correction and double-error detection.

reed-solomon.title: Reed-Solomon Codes
reed-solomon.define: Block codes over finite fields that correct symbol errors and erasures.
reed-solomon.notes: An (n,k) Reed-Solomon code has distance n-k+1; it can correct errors e and erasures s when 2e+s <= n-k.

ldpc.title: LDPC Codes
ldpc.define: Linear codes specified by sparse parity-check matrices and commonly decoded iteratively.

distance.title: Minimum Hamming Distance
distance.define: The smallest number of differing positions between distinct codewords.
distance.notes: A code of distance d can detect up to d-1 errors or uniquely correct up to floor((d-1)/2) errors under the corresponding decoding model.

arq.title: Retransmission (ARQ)
arq.define: Request another transmission when an error or missing acknowledgment is detected.
arq.notes: ARQ is a reliability protocol, not a forward error-correcting code.

symmetric.title: Symmetric Encryption
symmetric.define: Use a shared secret key for encryption and decryption.
symmetric.example: AES is a block cipher; ChaCha20 is a stream cipher.
symmetric.notes: A cipher must be used within a suitable construction or mode.

asymmetric.title: Public-Key Cryptography
asymmetric.define: Use related public and private keys for operations such as encryption, signatures, and key establishment.
asymmetric.notes: Not every public-key algorithm supports every operation.

public-encryption.title: Public-Key Encryption
public-encryption.define: Encrypt for a recipient using a public key; decrypt using the corresponding private key.
public-encryption.example: RSA-OAEP is a public-key encryption scheme.

key-agreement.title: Key Agreement
key-agreement.define: Establish shared key material through a cryptographic exchange.
key-agreement.notes: Key agreement needs authentication to resist an active intermediary.

hash.title: Cryptographic Hashing
hash.define: Map arbitrary-length messages to fixed-length digests with security properties such as collision resistance.
hash.notes: Hashing is not encryption and has no decryption key. An unkeyed hash alone does not authenticate the sender.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.define: Verify a claimed identity or the origin of data using a protocol and trusted key bindings.

mac.title: Message Authentication Code
mac.define: Use a shared secret key to produce a tag for message integrity and origin authentication.
mac.example: HMAC combines a cryptographic hash with a secret key.
mac.notes: Anyone holding the shared key can generate valid tags.

signature.title: Digital Signatures
signature.define: Sign with a private key and verify with the associated public key.
signature.notes: Verification establishes a key-based claim; identifying the signer requires a trusted binding from identity to public key. Signatures do not encrypt the message.

aead.title: Authenticated Encryption
aead.define: Combine confidentiality with integrity and authentication of ciphertext and associated data.
aead.notes: Associated data is authenticated but not encrypted. Nonce requirements depend on the scheme.

line-coding.title: Line Coding
line-coding.define: Map bits to baseband signal levels or transitions suitable for a link.

nrz.title: Non-Return-to-Zero (NRZ)
nrz.define: Represent bits using signal levels that need not return to a baseline between bits.
nrz.notes: Long runs without transitions can complicate clock recovery.

manchester.title: Manchester Coding
manchester.define: Represent each bit with a mid-bit transition; transition direction identifies the bit.
manchester.notes: Supports clock recovery with a bandwidth tradeoff; polarity conventions differ.

block-transmission.title: Block Transmission Coding
block-transmission.define: Map data blocks to constrained transmission symbols for properties such as transition density and DC balance.

8b10b.title: 8b/10b
8b10b.define: Map 8-bit data values to 10-bit transmission symbols with running-disparity control.
8b10b.notes: The data-bit/code-bit rate is 0.8. Added bits mainly support signaling constraints; this is not a general error-correction scheme.

digital-modulation.title: Digital Modulation
digital-modulation.define: Map discrete symbols to carrier waveforms for transmission.

ask.title: Amplitude-Shift Keying (ASK)
ask.define: Represent discrete symbols by selecting carrier amplitudes.

fsk.title: Frequency-Shift Keying (FSK)
fsk.define: Represent discrete symbols by selecting carrier frequencies.

psk.title: Phase-Shift Keying (PSK)
psk.define: Represent discrete symbols by selecting carrier phases.

qam.title: Quadrature Amplitude Modulation
qam.define: Represent symbols using combinations of in-phase and quadrature amplitudes.
qam.example: 16-QAM has 16 constellation points and can label each symbol with 4 bits.
qam.notes: This is a nominal mapping; net payload rate also depends on coding and protocol overhead.

analog-modulation.title: Analog Modulation
analog-modulation.define: Vary a carrier parameter continuously according to an analog message.
analog-modulation.notes: Analog modulation is included as a neighboring concept; it does not inherently start from bits.

am.title: Amplitude Modulation (AM)
am.define: Vary carrier amplitude according to an analog message.

fm.title: Frequency Modulation (FM)
fm.define: Vary instantaneous carrier frequency according to an analog message.

pm.title: Phase Modulation (PM)
pm.define: Vary carrier phase according to an analog message.

edges.value: removes redundancy; contrasted with adding redundancy
